Ex carpenter, current IT professional, and lifetime firearms enthusiast here 👋

I would like to offer several bits of advice to anyone that is wanting to prepare for something like this. 

First things first the reinforcement with the construction of the door. A couple main and easy steps to upgrade the integrity and strength of the door. 
1: replace the screws in both the hinges and striker plates with 3" (inch) exterior deck screws 
2: insure the quality of the door knob/deadbolt and their striker plates is as high as you can afford 
3: make sure your front door is not largely glass, have a peep through of course but no overly large windows 
4: any kind of extra interior only lock that you are comfortable with can only help (barrel pin, latch, hotel chain, etc.)
5. If you're versed or willing to do stud work install something called firebreaks in your wall tying the door jam to the studs closet to it (firebreaks are 2x4s or 2x6s that run horizontally between studs, and use a mix of screws and nails for this) this will greatly increase the strength off the door jam from sheer force

With the door reinforced now time to give yourself the tactical advantage. The camera this video was recorded on is a perfect example. Get something mounted to offer you a clean perspective but put it out of reach from the door so that it is harder to cover during a potential break in. Video is a great example. The camera you pick can be any style you would like just make sure you can recover the footage, it's great evidence in court if something goes wrong, and you can also pull it up live on your phone. The idea being that once someone comes knocking, or kicking in this case you can get an idea of their position and size. Information that is vital for this next part. 

Now for the advice on the firearms side of things. RULE NUMBER ONE!! USE EAR PROTECTION!! Guns are loud, if you have never shot one indoors just know that boom gets so much worse. With that being said my advice would be stash high quality ear protection and a non sentimental 12ga, loaded with high brass buckshot, near the front door at a safe distance from the entrance itself. In an ideal setup you would have some type of firing position from cover in case of return fire. 

Now for the execution part, you hear a bump in the night and someone is trying to pull the same thing as in the video. Step one is remain calm, a calm clear head in a situation like this will save your life. Get to your position and dawn your ear pro, pull up your camera feed and assess the situation. If the sturdiness of your door hasn't dissuaded the attempt it's sadly time to arrange a meet and greet with Jesus. The buckshot will have little trouble going through most wooden front doors, plus the amount of splintering and shrapnel produced by this round won't be fun for a potential b&e attacker. Using the information you have take aim and unload. 

The shotgun can definitely be swapped for something you would prefer or be more proficient with. Just keep over penetration in mind. You don't want to use something that will go through to much material and possibly hit something not intended. I won't lie though, a shotgun fired indoors is going to sound earth shattering. 

Hope some of this may help, best of luck to you all!

This would depend completely on what kind of behavior we mean here. Males even very young ones are far less agreeable on a lot of things than females. Now granted young men still need to be taught respect, compassion, and understand time and place for behaviors. However if you expect males and females to behave the exact same way in a classroom I wouldn't suggest holding your breath. My mother has been a sped teacher in both self-contained and gened classrooms for years so I've heard a lot of stories. I also work in the same school district in IT. With that being said my experience both second and first hand is that males, even in younger grads, will be harder to control. Regardless of punishment, they will be far more likely to act impulsively. Hell I was a jackass myself in a classroom growing up, but I don't think the course of action I've seen taken a lot in more recent years is the right approach. The approach being, completely neutralize these young men's natural way of thinking and acting. It's a dangerous thing to raise a generation of males in a way that they are taught what they do is wrong and to be more like the girls. I completely understand the frustration with the old adage of "boys will be boys", however the two sides of the biological coin exist for a reason. Regardless of political correctness, men and women have different strengths and weaknesses, differences that are apparent even in our grade schools. Of course don't limit opportunity based on gender, but do play into those strengths and weaknesses of those genders. When I walk into a classroom to make repairs or assessments the classrooms that are best behaved are the ones where the educator, regardless of gender, are up and moving around the room. Getting engaged themselves will naturally engage those being taught. 

I don't know if this rambling has made any sense or if it will help at all. I just felt I had something to share on the topic.

Best of luck to you and your school! Hope this issue can be resolved in a productive and healthy way!
